product_family: Postman API Platform (API Client, Spec Hub, Mock Servers, Collection Runner, Monitors, API Catalog, Insights) plus AI features (AI Engineer, Agent Mode, Postbot), Postman CLI, Postman MCP Server, and Enterprise add-ons (Advanced Security Administration: BYOK, Secret Scanner, Vault)

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type 2
certifications.proof_quote: SOC 2 Type 2 listed in Regulatory Compliance and Standards section of trust portal; corroborated by vendor blog: 'We kicked off the Type 2 audit period in September of 2020. The audit period ended on February 28, 2021' and Postman received 'the audit report with a favorable opinion.'

certifications.name: SOC 3
certifications.proof_quote: "SOC 3" listed as a Regulatory Compliance and Standards badge on the Customer Trust Portal.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022
certifications.proof_quote: "ISO/IEC 27001" and "ISO/IEC 27001:2022" (and a separately labeled "Certi-Trust ISO 27001") listed as certification badges on the Customer Trust Portal.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 27017:2015 (cloud security)
certifications.proof_quote: "ISO/IEC 27017:2015" listed as a certification badge on the Customer Trust Portal.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 (AI management system / AI governance)
certifications.proof_quote: "ISO/IEC 42001:2023" listed as a certification badge on the Customer Trust Portal, alongside SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: "Postman's baseline Enterprise security controls now independently satisfy HIPAA's technical safeguards without ASA add-ons" and Postman offers to sign 'a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for our HIPAA-covered customers.' Also listed as a badge on the Customer Trust Portal.

certifications.name: GDPR (posture, not a certification)
certifications.proof_quote: "Postman complies with the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (EU-U.S. DPF), the UK Extension to the DPF (UK DPF Extension), and the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (Swiss DPF)." GDPR is also listed as a Regulatory Compliance badge on the trust portal, and the Privacy Policy documents GDPR legal-basis processing.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: "PCI DSS" listed as a Regulatory Compliance and Standards badge on the trust portal and security page.

certifications.name: CSA STAR (Cloud Security Alliance)
certifications.proof_quote: "The Cloud Security Alliance's STAR Registry" / "CSA STAR" listed on the security page and trust portal.

certifications.name: CCPA (posture, not a certification)
certifications.proof_quote: "We do not sell your data for commercial purposes or 'share' data as defined under the CCPA and CPRA." Also listed as a badge on the trust portal.

certifications.name: TX-RAMP (Texas state risk/authorization program)
certifications.proof_quote: "TX-RAMP" listed as a Regulatory Compliance and Standards badge on the Customer Trust Portal.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: FedRAMP does not appear in the Regulatory Compliance and Standards section of Postman's Customer Trust Portal, which lists SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 42001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, CCPA, and TX-RAMP. Third-party aggregator sites claim FedRAMP compliance, but this is not corroborated on postman.com or security.postman.com, and Postman does not appear in the FedRAMP Marketplace.

privacy.ai_training_note: The Privacy Policy states: 'We may also use information you provide to develop artificial intelligence (AI) tools and systems as set forth in our Postman AI Terms.' The Security page states: 'Postman does not use customer data in internal testing. All validation and QA efforts are conducted on a production-mirrored internal stack using fictitious data only,' though that statement is scoped to internal QA/testing rather than AI feature training (Postbot, AI Engineer, Agent Mode).
privacy.data_region: Product data and backups hosted on AWS servers in the EU and the U.S.; Enterprise customers can use Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) to manage their own encryption keys.

security.name: Encryption at rest
security.value: AES-256-GCM for data at rest; sensitive data (environment variables, secrets, access tokens) encrypted at the application layer and managed via a key management system (KMS). Enterprise customers can enable Bring Your Own Key (BYOK).

security.name: Access control
security.value: Role-based access control (RBAC) and multi-factor authentication (MFA) cited as baseline Enterprise controls supporting HIPAA technical safeguards; Azure AD SCIM user provisioning also supported.

security.name: Tenant isolation
security.value: Tenant isolation and governed access to production systems cited as baseline Enterprise controls.

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: Application Penetration Testing and Network Penetration Testing reports available (gated) via the Customer Trust Portal.

security.name: Data storage redundancy
security.value: "All user data is encrypted and stored across six copies in three locations."

products.name: Postman API Platform (Free / Basic / Professional)
products.data_scope: API requests, collections, environments, workspace content; may be private or public workspaces
products.notes: Core product available to individuals and small teams; SOC 2 and ISO certifications apply to the shared platform infrastructure.

products.name: Postman Enterprise
products.category: API governance and platform at scale
products.data_scope: Same workspace content plus admin/org-level controls, SCIM provisioning, audit logs
products.notes: Baseline Enterprise security controls now independently satisfy HIPAA technical safeguards without requiring the ASA add-on, per Postman's own 2026 HIPAA compliance announcement.

products.name: Advanced Security Administration (ASA) add-on
products.data_scope: Encryption keys (BYOK), scanned secrets, vaulted credentials
products.notes: Includes Bring Your Own Key (BYOK), Secret Scanner, and Vault. Formerly required for HIPAA compliance; now optional/'a plus' rather than mandatory per the vendor's 2026 blog post.

products.name: AI Engineer / Agent Mode / Postbot
products.data_scope: Workspace and API context is used to ground AI suggestions
products.notes: Governed by the separate Postman AI Terms. The Privacy Policy states user-provided information may be used to develop Postman's AI tools and systems, which differs in scope from the security page's statement that customer data is not used in internal testing (that statement covers QA rather than AI training).

products.name: Postman Public API Network / MCP Server Catalog
products.data_scope: Publicly published APIs, docs, and MCP server listings
products.notes: Public-by-design; not in scope for confidential customer data handling.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium SaaS (Free tier, paid Basic/Professional tiers, custom-priced Enterprise tier with add-ons)
compare.data_residency: AWS data centers in the EU and the U.S.; no additional regional hosting options are documented in vendor materials.

flags: AI training posture: the Privacy Policy states customer-provided information may be used 'to develop artificial intelligence (AI) tools and systems as set forth in our Postman AI Terms,' while the Security page states customer data is not used in 'internal testing.' These are different scopes, AI feature training versus QA, and the AI Terms document does not spell out which controls apply to AI Engineer, Agent Mode, and Postbot.
FedRAMP is claimed by several third-party aggregator sites (not Postman-owned) but does not appear on Postman's own Customer Trust Portal certification list.

The Customer Trust Portal (security.postman.com) gates most underlying audit reports and documents (SOC 2 report, penetration test reports, DPA) behind a 'Get access' / request flow; only the certification labels themselves are publicly visible without a request.
